cadence_normalization_instructions:
Parse cadence expressions into ISO 8601 duration format. Handle various formats:
Seconds: "12 s" PT12S
Minutes: "5 minutes" PT5M
Hours: "2 hours" PT2H
Days: "1 day" P1D
Range: "12–16 s" PT12S/PT16S
Fractional: "0.5 seconds" PT0.5S
Frequency: "5 Hz" PT0.2S
Multiple cadences: "3 second and 1 minute" PT3S, PT1M
Unclear: "High cadence" NONE
No cadence info: "The instrument measured particles" NONE
Averaged data product: "Distributions averaged to 1-hour to match ACE/SWICS" PT1H When data is "averaged to X" or has "X cadence", extract X - this is the temporal resolution of the data product used
Averaged data product: "1-hour cadence heavy-ion charge state ratios" PT1H Extract the stated cadence of the data product
Averaged data product: "Yearly averages of daily solar wind data" P1Y The output cadence is yearly, even though input is daily
Analysis window (NOT cadence): "Regression with 27-day averages" NONE 27 days is an analysis/averaging window for statistical processing, not the measurement cadence
Event duration (NOT cadence): "10-hour southward IMF Bz interval" NONE 10 hours describes event duration, not measurement frequency
Frequency with rounding: "11 Hz measurements" PT0.090909S 1/11 = 0.090909... Round to 6 decimal places
Return ONLY the ISO 8601 duration string(s), nothing else: - Single cadence: PT3S - Multiple cadences: PT3S, PT1M - Range: PT12S/PT16S - Cannot determine: NONE
Do NOT include any JSON, explanations, or notes. Just the duration string(s) or "NONE".
Always output ISO 8601 duration format (PT for time, P for days/months/years) Support plural and singular units (e.g., "sec", "second", "seconds") If range is provided, express it as "PT12S/PT16S" If cadence is a frequency (Hz), convert to period in seconds Round fractional seconds to maximum 6 decimal places (e.g., 1/11 Hz = PT0.090909S, not PT0.0909090909S) If multiple distinct cadences, separate with comma and space If value cannot be determined from text, return "NONE" NEVER guess a cadence; return "NONE" if uncertain Extract "averaged to X" or "X cadence" data products - this is the temporal resolution used in analysis Do NOT extract analysis windows (e.g., "27-day averages in regression") or event durations (e.g., "10-hour interval") - return "NONE" for these Return ONLY the duration string(s) or "NONE" - no other text
1 minute = 60 seconds 1 hour = 3600 seconds 1 day = 86400 seconds Hz to seconds = 1 / frequency
